title: GraphQL security runner: introspection abuse, query depth attacks, field suggestion, injection via GraphQL
goal: GraphQL is increasingly prevalent in modern APIs. ZAP and Nuclei have limited GraphQL-specific testing. Implement a graphql-probe runner: (1) Discovery: detect GraphQL endpoints (/graphql, /api/graphql, /v1/graphql, /gql). Check for GraphQL playground/IDE exposure (/graphiql, /playground). (2) Introspection enabled: send __schema introspection query. If successful → enumerate all types, queries, mutations, fields. Finding: 'GraphQL Introspection Enabled - Full Schema Disclosed'. Generate a schema map for subsequent tests. (3) Query depth attack (DoS prevention): send deeply nested query (10+ levels). Check if server applies depth limiting. If not → 'GraphQL Missing Query Depth Limit'. (4) Field suggestion leakage: send a query with a typo (e.g., 'user' as 'usr'). If server suggests 'Did you mean user?' → field enumeration without introspection. (5) SQL/NoSQL injection via GraphQL: inject SQL payloads into string arguments (id: '1 OR 1=1'). (6) Batching attack: send array of multiple queries in one request to bypass rate limiting. (7) Authorization bypass: test if unauthenticated queries can access data restricted to authenticated users via type confusion. Active tier. Tool: graphw00f for detection, graphql-cop for security checks, or custom Python.
scope: API security gap analysis: GraphQL is not specifically covered. As modern apps increasingly use GraphQL (GitHub, Shopify, Facebook APIs), this is a critical coverage gap for API-first assessments.
generation_reason: GraphQL security not covered — introspection, injection, depth attacks are standard GraphQL pentest checks. Critical for API security tile assessments.
